parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: B1: state or imply 4y(dy/dx) as the derivative of 2y². B1: state or imply 3x(dy/dx) + 3y as the derivative of 3xy; if d/dx is introduced in place of dy/dx, allow B1 for both followed by a correct method, maximum 2. M1: differentiate all four terms, collect or bracket both dy/dx terms and solve; when all terms are included this must be an equation. A1 AG: obtain dy/dx = (2x − 3y − 1)/(4y + 3x), having shown (4y + 3x)dy/dx = 2x − 3y − 1 or equivalent. If '= 2x' or '= 0' is not used consistently, M1 A0 with no recovery. Allow full marks using dx and dy. [Total: 4]

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The stationary-condition equation has no real roots, so no tangent is parallel to the $x$-axis.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: M1*: equate the numerator to zero, obtain 2x = 3y + 1, and form an equation in x only or y only from 2y² + 3xy + x = x²; errors are allowed. DM1: obtain a three-term quadratic and try to solve, e.g. 17x² − 8x + 2 = 0 or 17y² + 6y + 1 = 0; if the formulation has errors, allow the usual quadratic-solution method mark. A1 CWO: conclude that the equation has no real roots, using a negative discriminant, e.g. −72 or −32. [Total: 3]
